domain.name: Multi-hop Fact Verification
domain.content_type: Claims to verify against Wikipedia abstracts through iterative retrieval
domain.task_complexity: Requires chaining multiple retrieval steps to gather evidence, resolving entity references across documents, identifying missing critical evidence, and determining claim veracity through reasoning over disconnected passages

domain_terminology.meaning: Process of performing exactly three sequential document retrievals to gather evidence
A statement to be verified as true or false using retrieved passages
Retrieved Wikipedia abstracts that may contain evidence for verification
Step-by-step logical analysis connecting claim elements to passage evidence
Conclusion about claim veracity or identification of missing evidence needed
Specific passages that directly support or refute claim components

common_error_patterns.name: premature_verification
common_error_patterns.description: Concluding claim is verified/refuted without all necessary evidence

common_error_patterns.name: entity_confusion
common_error_patterns.description: Incorrectly matching entities with similar names or properties
detection_hints: conflating different works with similar titles

common_error_patterns.name: missing_bridging_evidence
common_error_patterns.description: Having evidence for endpoints but missing the connection between them
detection_hints: knowing actor's nationality and film existence, but not which film the actor was in
missing 'who starred in' or 'who wrote' connections

common_error_patterns.name: transitive_reasoning_failure
common_error_patterns.description: Failing to chain evidence across multiple documents (A→B, B→C, therefore A→C)
detection_hints: having passage about 'star of Dirty O'Neil' and separate passage about 'actor in 1982 film' but not connecting them

common_error_patterns.name: false_nationality_claim
common_error_patterns.description: Claim states wrong nationality/origin for person or entity
detection_hints: claim says 'South American' but evidence shows 'American'
claim says 'Welsh' but evidence shows different origin

common_error_patterns.name: irrelevant_passage_distraction
common_error_patterns.description: Retrieved passages contain related entities but don't address the specific claim
detection_hints: passages about different films/books with similar themes

common_error_patterns.name: insufficient_evidence_not_flagged
common_error_patterns.description: System doesn't identify when critical evidence is missing from retrieved passages
detection_hints: passages discuss related topics but don't contain the specific facts needed
no passage linking entity A to entity B

correctness_criteria.description: All entities and relationships in claim must be verified through retrieved passages
correctness_criteria.how_to_verify: Trace each claim component to supporting passage text; identify any gaps

correctness_criteria.description: All entities (people, places, works) must be correctly identified and matched
correctness_criteria.how_to_verify: Check names, nationalities, dates, and relationships match exactly between claim and evidence

correctness_criteria.description: System must recognize when passages are insufficient for verification
correctness_criteria.how_to_verify: Explicit statement of what evidence is missing and what would be needed to verify

correctness_criteria.description: Reasoning must follow valid logical steps without unsupported inferences
correctness_criteria.how_to_verify: Each reasoning step should cite specific passage content; no assumptions

correctness_criteria.description: Every assertion in the claim must be addressed (conjunctions, qualifiers, etc.)
correctness_criteria.how_to_verify: Parse claim into atomic facts; verify each is addressed in reasoning
